routes.title: I am starting with no computing background
routes.introduction: Begin with everyday ideas and paper activities. No installation is required. Read at your own pace; a learner can speak, draw or write an answer.

steps.title: Computing from the Beginning
steps.purpose: Eight lessons from following a page to understanding what an operating system does.

steps.title: Inside a computer
steps.purpose: Meet physical components after practising input, rules and output.

steps.title: Bits and digital logic
steps.purpose: Explore how a shared interpretation turns patterns into information.

steps.title: The processor and memory
steps.purpose: Follow a sequence of instructions and distinguish working memory from storage.

routes.title: I want to write my first program
routes.introduction: First practise giving clear instructions. Then learn one command environment and one language. Reading the concepts does not require installing every tool.

steps.title: C from the Beginning
steps.purpose: Eleven small steps from reading a program to checking functions and borrowed memory, with an optional prepared-toolchain lab.

steps.title: Turn a problem into steps
steps.purpose: Develop an algorithm, choose examples and predict results.

steps.title: Commands in PowerShell
steps.purpose: Use this route on Windows; understand the working folder and each command before running it.

steps.title: Commands in Bash
steps.purpose: An alternative shell route for a suitable environment, not a prerequisite to finish PowerShell.

steps.title: Write a program in C
steps.purpose: Learn source code, functions and values through a note-saving program.

steps.title: Write safer C23
steps.purpose: Practise checking inputs and errors before a systems lab.

steps.title: Pointers and borrowed memory
steps.purpose: Prepare for buffer and lifetime discussions in the Kernel course.

steps.title: Compilers, CMake and tests
steps.purpose: Understand which stage prepares, compiles, links or checks a program.

routes.title: I want to understand Umicom OS
routes.introduction: Umicom OS includes a Linux-based image foundation and Framework-backed user-space software. Begin with its role, then read the course's source exercises. Hosted lab checks do not establish that a guest or physical computer boots.

steps.title: Meet the Umicom projects
steps.purpose: Understand why reusable Framework services and applications are separate.

steps.title: The system above the kernel
steps.purpose: Connect files, processes and services to the purpose of an OS.

steps.title: Prepare a development computer
steps.purpose: Use only when ready for practical builds; check current repository prerequisites.

steps.title: Umicom OS from Scratch
steps.purpose: Initial source-reading and hosted labs on startup plans, recovery, image identity and guest checks.

steps.title: System administration
steps.purpose: Learn the distinction between using a system and managing its configuration.

routes.title: I want to understand Umicom Kernel
routes.introduction: The native Kernel is a separate project. Follow the first four sections of the foundation route and introductory C before its practical exercises. Use the subject links below to return to a concept as it appears in the source.

steps.title: What a kernel does
steps.purpose: Understand privilege and the difference between the host and target machine.

steps.title: From the first instruction to a kernel
steps.purpose: Follow the startup idea before studying machine-specific details.

steps.title: Umicom Kernel from Scratch
steps.purpose: Read and exercise bounded input and firmware-memory contracts using real Kernel source.

steps.title: Boot and inspect the research Kernel
steps.purpose: A later, tool-dependent exercise; follow the exact supported machine profile.

steps.title: Memory management in the source
steps.purpose: Connect locations, page ownership and translation.

steps.title: Privilege and traps
steps.purpose: Understand controlled entry when execution needs Kernel attention.

steps.title: Messages between processes
steps.purpose: IPC means inter-process communication; follow who owns each message.

steps.title: Scheduling and waiting
steps.purpose: Study how a process waits for work and later resumes.

steps.title: Timers and events
steps.purpose: Follow timed work and the event owner.

steps.title: Interrupts and recovery
steps.purpose: Read the response to interruptions and faults.

steps.title: Drivers and interrupt boundaries
steps.purpose: Connect the device to the software responsible for it.

steps.title: Device requests
steps.purpose: Trace a request through completion, timeout and reset.

steps.title: Device discovery
steps.purpose: Compare firmware information with supported device bindings.

steps.title: Filesystems and storage
steps.purpose: Connect named files to storage and ownership.

bridges.title: Read a native kernel without booting it
bridges.purpose: Compare the host exercise with the actual native Kernel responsibilities.

bridges.title: A system has several layers
bridges.purpose: Connect this overview to the OS startup source and its separate owners.

bridges.title: Hosted Kernel labs
bridges.purpose: Study bounded input and firmware contracts before machine boot experiments.

bridges.title: Keep firmware-owned pages out of the allocator
bridges.purpose: Connect page ownership to the boot reservation planner.

bridges.title: Read firmware bytes without following their addresses
bridges.purpose: Follow the shared device-tree reader before interpreting device bindings.

bridges.title: A byte span is not a string
bridges.purpose: Apply bounds and lifetime ideas to Kernel input.

bridges.title: Reject overflow before multiplying
bridges.purpose: Compare checked arithmetic across financial and system-input domains.

bridges.title: Build one real OS component
bridges.purpose: Use the toolchain concepts in a small hosted lab.

bridges.title: Read the native Kernel source
bridges.purpose: Distinguish host checks from target-machine execution.

bridges.title: What does a computer do?
bridges.purpose: Return to the input, instruction and result model before the component details.

bridges.title: C from the Beginning
bridges.purpose: Begin with one greeting, values and decisions before the note-saving program.
